The data doesn't settle direction. Residual_u10m and Residual_sea_ice are only weakly correlated (r ≈ 0.07), and nonlinear fits are just as weak in both directions. So I'm relying on physical reasoning. Surface wind pushes sea ice around and changes its coverage, while sea ice has little direct influence on the large-scale 10 m wind. That makes B the more likely relationship.

ANSWER: B
